title: Transfer-Associated Delay to Arterial Puncture Within the London Thrombectomy Network: A Retrospective Observational Analysis of Direct and Transferred Thrombectomy Pathways
content: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is highly time-sensitive, and early reperfusion after large-vessel occlusion stroke improves functional outcome. Interhospital transfer broadens access to MT but adds delay. We examined whether transfer dependency is associated with delayed arterial puncture within the London thrombectomy network, and identified operational contributors to delay. This was a retrospective observational analysis of aggregate Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme (SSNAP) data from all six thrombectomy-performing Hyperacute Stroke Units in London, April 2024–March 2025. Centre-level direct-admission and transferred referral-to-puncture intervals were compared; transfer-associated delay (TAD) was defined as their difference. Transferred pathways were decomposed into door-in-door-out (DIDO), conveyance, and receiving-centre door-to-puncture (DTP) intervals, with pre-specified leave-one-out sensitivity analysis. Of 934 thrombectomy procedures, 541 (57.9%) followed interhospital transfer. Transfer dependency varied almost tenfold (7.4–68.5%) and was strongly, inversely associated with TAD (r = −0.99, 95% CI −1.00 to −0.94, p < 0.001), an association that persisted after excluding the most extreme centre (r = −0.98). DIDO was uniformly prolonged (127–136 minutes), accounting for 37.6–59.9% of the transferred interval; receiving-centre DTP varied more than threefold (34–113 minutes) and correlated with TAD (r = 0.84, p = 0.036), but this association was not robust to exclusion of the most extreme centre (r = 0.34, p = 0.57). Whilst transfer resulted in substantial delays to thrombectomy, transfer dependency was not a significant contributor and instead was inversely related to delay. Prolonged DIDO presents the most consistent operational factor towards thrombectomy delay and is an appropriate generalizable target for network-wide quality improvement.
